elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Rendered: "This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York." replacing Nova Scotia/Canada law.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Rendered: "exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York, except that either party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any court of competent jurisdiction." The carve-out is limited to temporary injunctive relief, which preserves the exclusive merits forum.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Rendered clause selects New York law, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. Not a defect—preferred level is satisfied instead.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Forum is New York County state and federal courts, not Delaware/California/London. Not a defect—preferred level is satisfied instead.

reasons: Both preferred elements are met in operative language: New York governing law plus exclusive New York County state and federal court jurisdiction with a carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief, which per the rule boundaries preserves the exclusive merits forum.

Minimal: only the jurisdiction and forum words were changed (Nova Scotia law/non-exclusive Nova Scotia courts to New York law/exclusive New York County courts), the two-sentence structure and remaining wording are retained, and the injunctive-relief carve-out is required by the second preferred element rather than an extra.
Preserves intent: no undefined terms, dangling cross-references, or contradictory retained sentences; the clause was the sole governing-law/venue provision and no arbitration clause is displaced.
Fallback elements are unmet only because the drafter targeted the preferred level; position-completeness is satisfied at the preferred level.
Severity retained at medium: the original Nova Scotia clause was outside the accepted list but venue was non-exclusive, so deviation rather than walk-away.
